newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army says 300 rebels killed in April.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army says 300 rebels killed in April.

text.p: Burundi's army said on Wednesday troops killed at least 300 Hutu rebels in southern Burundi in April after up to 3,000 rebels attacked from Tanzania.
Army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi said rebels on Tuesday night attacked a secondary school in Bururi province in the south and killed 30 people and wounded many others.
Nibizi said the army had only lost six of its soldiers in fighting with the rebels in the south since April 5 when between 2,000 and 3,000 Hutu rebels launched an attack from bases inside Tanzania.

The spokesman said many houses in the southern provinces of Makamba and Bururi had been set ablaze by the rebels and a national radio transmitter was damaged. He said rebel forces were now trying to infiltrate into three communes in Bururi.
But he added the border between southern Burundi and northwestern Tanzania was now tightly controlled so it would be hard for the rebels to return to their safe haven in Tanzania.
More than 150,000 people, mostly civilians, have been killed in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and rebels since troops killed Burundi's first Hutu president in 1993.
Burundian Hutu rebels of the National Council for the Defence of Democracy were uprooted from their bases in Zaire last year when Zairean Tutsi-dominated rebels seized the area.
